[[Category:Critical thinking]][[Category:Philosophical method]]
[[File:Critical thinking.png|thumbnail|Think critically to avoid being misled.]]
'''Critical thinking''' is the practice of carefully analysing

* [[information]]
* [[belief]]s
* [[argument]]s

to 

* make well-reasoned decisions
* form justified beliefs
* avoid being misled

<ref>{{#cite:Q2791}}</ref>

== Applications ==

=== In [[philosophy]] ===

==== Necessity ====

* Philosophical ideas are often imperfect
** they may be valid in some scenarios, but not others. 
* Generalisations or further inferences may lead to uncomfortable conclusions
* Many philosophical answers may have been proposed on the same topic, each with its strength and weaknesses. 
** The best understanding is often via a combination of multiple perspectives and models.

<ref>{{#cite:Q1837}}</ref>

==== Method ====

===== Considering logical consequences =====

For instance:

* '''Idea to critically analyse''': past events fully determine the future.
* '''Logical consequence to consider''': free will is an illusion.

<ref>{{#cite:Q1837}}</ref>
